tradition.name: Early music ensemble
tradition.lineage: Fretwork and Iestyn Davies — complete dated Purcell & Nyman: Music After Awhile concert programme,29October2019,Christ Church Cathedral,Vancouver. Presenter programme names Davies countertenor,Asako Morikawa and Emily Ashton treble viols,Joanna Levine tenor viol,Sam Stadlen and Richard Boothby bass viols. Five instrumentalists and one singer,three viol registers preserved in one explicitly composite consort owner. Whole programme includes Purcell fantasias and songs alongside contemporary Nyman commissions/arrangements. Complete event programme is the selected documented performance practice; linked presenter-issued If and Music for a While videos corroborate actual performance, not grounds for importing an unrelated album roster. No claim every musician sounds throughout every work; pre-concert discussion is not a musical speaker part. Authored modern concert rendition of the complete source palette,one accompanied voice plus mixed-register viol consort. Consort construction follows Viola da Gamba Society guidance: fretted bowed instruments,underhand bow grip and plain upper gut/silver-wound lower gut strings; this is explicit generic physical realization rather than measured Fretwork instrument makes or actual winding metals (silver is an authored choice). Wood species,bow-stick species,exact strings per instrument,concert pitch and temperament remain unspecified. Neutral vocal physiology remains unspecified despite the source countertenor label. Classical legato bow gesture,unprocessed one-lead voice and treated live-room capture are authored rendering choices,not a transcription of every articulation or measured cathedral acoustics; this is a fresh authored recording rendition, not venue reconstruction. No signal-chain hardware or global tuning imposed.

tradition.name: Indonesian indigenous traditional
tradition.lineage: Singers of Desa Gemar Baru / Kenyah Umaq Jalan — Dance Song, complete7:44 Smithsonian1998track SFW40444_101. Full original Smithsonian field notes specify Pekulung soloist with a chorus of22women and14men:37singers in total. The selected complete seven-verse recorded song was commissioned with the singers seated on the floor, not recorded during dancing. Only voices are positively specified for this track; sampeq duets are separately discussed recordings on volume13, not omitted accompaniment here. The website partial performer metadata is not treated as exhaustive headcount; the detailed track-specific booklet supplies the complete37-person formation. No stamping card is added from discussion of a different dance-event context. The verses invite and conclude dancing, offer conventional advice and narrate dispersal at the end of the evening. This broad Indonesian indigenous-tradition field includes documented Kenyah communal vocal poetry beyond actual existing Javanese/Balinese instrumental gamelan, shaken angklung and Sundanese-specific repertoire. No claim these regional traditions are mutually unrelated or exhaust national heritage. The selected source is explicitly Kenyah Umaq Jalan, with formally described solo-and-chorus verse practice, pentatonic melody without semitones and frequent parallel thirds/fourths/fifths. It does not imply all Indonesian indigenous music shares this texture or scale. Broad balladPoetry follows the complete unaccompanied poetic/narrative verses; communal37-person scale is retained rather than pretending a solo intimate singer. Parent does not assert functional chord progressions, a sustained drone, improvisation, worship or concert purpose. The source expressly leaves old-religion ritual usage uncertain; recreational celebration and historical church influence are not relabeled devotional worship. Source-neutral vocal physiology, single combined live ensemble and moderate effort are authored controls. Exact interval frequencies, singer ranges and microphones are not given; global temperament and recording chain are omitted. Controlled live-room rendition is editorial, not the original floor-seated site.

instrument_role_audit.rationale: Full original Smithsonian field notes specify Pekulung soloist with a chorus of22women and14men:37singers in total. The selected complete seven-verse recorded song was commissioned with the singers seated on the floor, not recorded during dancing. Only voices are positively specified for this track; sampeq duets are separately discussed recordings on volume13, not omitted accompaniment here. The website partial performer metadata is not treated as exhaustive headcount; the detailed track-specific booklet supplies the complete37-person formation. No stamping card is added from discussion of a different dance-event context. The verses invite and conclude dancing, offer conventional advice and narrate dispersal at the end of the evening. This broad Indonesian indigenous-tradition field includes documented Kenyah communal vocal poetry beyond actual existing Javanese/Balinese instrumental gamelan, shaken angklung and Sundanese-specific repertoire. No claim these regional traditions are mutually unrelated or exhaust national heritage. The selected source is explicitly Kenyah Umaq Jalan, with formally described solo-and-chorus verse practice, pentatonic melody without semitones and frequent parallel thirds/fourths/fifths. It does not imply all Indonesian indigenous music shares this texture or scale. Broad balladPoetry follows the complete unaccompanied poetic/narrative verses; communal37-person scale is retained rather than pretending a solo intimate singer. Parent does not assert functional chord progressions, a sustained drone, improvisation, worship or concert purpose. The source expressly leaves old-religion ritual usage uncertain; recreational celebration and historical church influence are not relabeled devotional worship. Source-neutral vocal physiology, single combined live ensemble and moderate effort are authored controls. Exact interval frequencies, singer ranges and microphones are not given; global temperament and recording chain are omitted. Controlled live-room rendition is editorial, not the original floor-seated site.

Japanese Traditional is a broader cross-lineage heritage field than existing shakuhachi_honkyoku, gagaku or other individually named historical traditions. The exact creator corpus includes koto performer Shinichi Yuize, Kyoto Imperial Court and Nippon Gagaku Kai, and Junko Ueda alongside Goro Yamaguchi. Independent Nonesuch Japanese catalogue positively describes separate koto schools and traditional vocal/instrumental and kabuki repertoires; breadth is not inferred merely from national artist birthplaces. The selected Kinko solo branch substantially overlaps shakuhachi_honkyoku; no claim it is a newly distinct flute technique. Existing japanese_classical describes a Western-derived composed-music branch, while ethnomusicology is cross-cultural documentary curation and Japanese Instrumental also includes modern jazz/pop. tradition.name: Japanese VTuber
tradition.lineage: Hoshimachi Suisei / Tsumiki — BIBBIDIBA, complete Miyuki Uchida Yamaha six-page solo-piano arrangement. Yamaha explicitly publishes the complete six-page intermediate solo-piano edition, composer/lyricist Tsumiki and arranger Miyuki Uchida. Its performance notes describe rhythmic left-hand motion, crisp short notes, selective pedal and a reworked accompaniment for the rap-like E section. This whole published arrangement is selected, not an isolated piano reduction claimed to reconstruct the original studio master. One piano performer covers melody and accompaniment; no separately notated singer is specified by the solo edition. The original song singer and composer are not counted as performers of this authored piano realization. Hololive directly identifies Hoshimachi Suisei as its virtual idol and its institutional VTuber production article explicitly identifies her collaboration with Tsumiki on BIBBIDIBA. Japanese VTuber describes the avatar-mediated streaming talent and creator institution, not a universal instrument palette. Actual existing vocaloid_synth_voice and vocaloid_producer_scene center synthesized voicebanks; shared creators do not make this talent institution identical to that production mechanism. Existing anime_cv centers anime-character songs and j_pop_classic the broad mainstream agency/pop lineage, both overlapping repertoire contexts but not synonymous with the VTuber institution. This selected published J-pop song arrangement uses broad functionalSong with an explicitly authored functional-harmonic verse/refrain realization, not a measured transcription claim about every original section and not art-music classification merely from notation. Steinway D nine-foot concert grand, block-chord pop keyboard articulation, modern piano wire/felt and equal temperament are authored representative construction choices, not claims about the original singer recording or Yamaha specifying that piano model. Controlled live-room capture is likewise authored.

One unaccompanied singer retained, no instruments or other album singers imported. The creator Moroccan Traditional playlist includes this exact artist/title/duration at21. Moroccan Traditional is a cross-community heritage field: the exact creator corpus spans Gnawa, Atlas/Amazigh ensembles, Aissawa, Andalusi-school musicians and Moroccan Jewish singers, including this performer. The Smithsonian collector independently documents a locally transmitted Tetuan repertoire, not merely an artist born in Morocco. Existing gnawa identifies a specific Sufi/West-African-derived ceremony; andalusi_nuba and andalusian_classical codified modal suite lineages; chaabi_moroccan and chaabi_marocain urban celebration traditions; moroccan_pop and classic_moroccan_pop commercial/crossover fields. Those remain overlapping constituent or neighboring repertoires, not excluded by their sample artists. Existing sephardi_bakkashot concerns specifically pre-dawn supplicatory liturgical singing, while this documented Ladino narrative romance belongs to a different domestic repertoire; neither it nor one Sephardi example exhausts the broader Moroccan field. tradition.name: Musica calabrese
tradition.lineage: Peppe Voltarelli — musical performances at the first Trame di Color Fest presentation of Voltarelli canta Profazio, reported by its organizer on 17 June 2016. The organizer describes his Calabrian dialect folk revival and quotes his voice-and-guitar-only stage practice; he sings Qua si campa d’aria, Amuri amuri and Allu mè paisi. This realization retains the complete two-role solo practice, one singer accompanying himself on guitar. Discussion moderator Andrea Di Consoli is not an additional musical singer; studio-album arrangements and absent Profazio are not imported into this live scope. Authored new recording of the complete documented solo format. A strummed steel-string dreadnought with Engelmann top, rosewood back and sides, standard tuning and 80/20 strings is an explicit recording choice for the source-generic guitar, not a claim about original construction. One accompanied singer uses neutral physiological controls and an authored small-note-group neumatic setting; exact source ornamentation is not measured. Broad balladPoetry reflects the positively documented lyric/dialect storytelling priority and sparse accompaniment, without an inferred specific Mediterranean mode. Live-room setting is authored; global tuning and capture hardware are unspecified.

tradition.lineage: Vitor Colares — complete eight-song música alheia (Mercúrio Música, 23 June 2020). The issuing label credits Vitor C. with voice and steel-string acoustic guitar, and Diego Maia only with mixing/mastering. The artist describes home-recorded acoustic versions of songs by fellow Ceará artists. All eight songs and both positively credited performing roles are retained; one singer. Listed songwriters and artwork contributors are not extra performers. No instrumentation of the original bands or the separate Clau Aniz/Vitor Colares duet is imported into these solo versions. Authored contemporary solo-song realization of the complete album: source-positive steel-string guitar is modeled by a strummed dreadnought with Engelmann top, rosewood back/sides, standard tuning and80/20strings. Exact size, woods, strings and strumming gesture are authored, not measured original gear. All17 human voice controls remain; a single accompanied singer uses source-unspecified physiology and an explicitly authored small-note-group neumatic setting. Broad functionalSong represents this authored recurring lyrical verse/refrain and chordal accompaniment, not an assertion that all Ceará music has the same form. Controlled live-room capture is an authored new recording environment; original source says recorded at home. Global tuning and recording apparatus are unspecified.

Retain four people and all four sound families across the complete album; doubled roles do not imply simultaneous playing by each person. Positive instrumental tags support zero singers. Generic percussion remains unidentified, not silently replaced by drum kit or invented hand drum. The album includes Chiapas, Los Parachicos and Sones Chiapanecos among a wider traditional Mexican/bolero book. Authored complete-album palette. Isolated Chiapanecan owner retains all three original physical/ensemble controls and source-positive regional identity; traditional grande/tenor ensemble and hormigo/wood resonators are editorial realization choices, not measured source construction. A2.5-octave plastic-mallet glockenspiel, long-scale alder soapbar bass with locked fingerstyle and source-unspecified credited percussion are authored choices; all actual source roles retained. Mexican song-form parent describes these arranged traditional son and bolero forms, including instrumental song renditions; no sung voice or exclusively dance function inferred. Controlled live room, no invented capture chain or global tuning.

tradition.name: Música pitiusa
tradition.lineage: Complete instrumental ball pagès practice specified in the2012 Consell d’Eivissa heritage inventory: a castanyoler and a sonador playing flaüta and tambor together, supporting the four named dances. Three sound-source roles, zero singer roles in the positive official performer inventory. The federation separately documents melodic fragment elaboration and rhythmic improvisation. This is a historical practice realization, not an assertion about every current performance; its complete2012instrument list excludes the espasí that the newer federation page identifies as a later dance-use addition from caramelles. No invented named performer or claim to a particular2025recording with placeholder credits. Authored controlled live-room recording of the complete documented instrumental practice. Broad improvOnFrame follows the source-positive oral melodic-fragment elaboration over dance metre; not jazz or an invented harmonic progression. Flaüta retains its oleander duct-flute body with three finger holes, operated one-handed beside the drum; exact tuning and metal inlay unspecified. Tambor retains a hollow pine body, two skin heads, rope tension and fibre buzzing cord; goat skin is selected from the documented goat/rabbit possibilities, not asserted universal. Large juniper castanyoles retain paired halves with separating badall and hand ties. Neutral numeric axes are editorial scaffolding. Existing Basque txistu, region-specific tabor and differently constructed concert/flamenco castanets are not silently relabeled; three isolated owners preserve regional identity without shared edits. Global temperament and capture hardware omitted.

tradition.name: Música rapa nui
tradition.lineage: Amahiro’s complete announced one-hour Tapu concert, Centro GAM,9January2017. Mario Ama Tuki sings and plays guitar; Vai a Tare Paoa sings backing vocals; Andrés K. Pakarati plays guitar; Te Uira Tuki bass; Moana Moulton Tepano drums; Carlos Campusano percussion. Retain all six performers, two singers and five sound-source families; the two positively electric guitar roles share one timbre-family card, not one invented guitarist. Sound technicians are not extra performers. Source-unspecified auxiliary percussion remains neutral. The festival identifies contemporary Rapa Nui repertoire combining island tradition with rock, folk and blues, performed in Rapa Nui, Spanish and English. This is the whole documented concert arrangement, not a claim to full Tapu studio overdubs. Authored recurring verse/refrain and tonal chord support for this contemporary song concert places the selected realization under functionalSong; this is not a measured analysis of every source song or the whole island repertoire. Two singers use a neutral live-duet configuration, without invented intervals, technique lineage or physiology. Electric guitars use authored alder bodies, maple necks, rosewood boards, AlnicoII single coils, pure-nickel10s and clean chordal strokes. Bass uses authored alder, fretted long scale, nickel roundwounds and soapbar pickups with locked fingerstyle. Thin maple drum kit with brushes and sticks and traditional-finish fully lathed machine-hammeredB20 cymbals is an authored supportive texture, not exact source inventory. Bare percussion credit receives no guessed subtype. Controlled live room is authored, not the source hall; global tuning and original recording apparatus omitted.

tradition.name: Música sudcaliforniana
tradition.lineage: Complete announced4July2025 Los Inalcanzables de la Baja concert at Parque Piedras y Pájaros, La Paz, for Festival Tuma Umutú. Presenter’s first-person release names current trio Marco Trasviña (tuba), Damián Avilés (guitar and voice), Juan Flores (requinto); Juan explicitly replaces historical film member Luis Fernando Olachea. Retain one positively credited singer and all three instrument roles. Six named film corridos plus further repertoire form the whole concert. Film itself is not selected: its independent score and historical personnel are not erased or mixed into this live trio. No second voice or extra drums inferred. FunctionalSong.mexican follows positively documented corrido and sierreña song repertoire. Authored neutral solo voice with syllabic delivery, single lead and no exact physiological training claims. Bare guitar is realized as mahogany OM steel-string, standard tuning and flatpicked accompaniment; these are editorial choices, not measured guitar construction. The separately credited requinto retains its specific role through an isolated neutral owner: body, stringing, tuning and exact playing method remain unspecified, with no Veracruz/jarocho identity or guessed nylon/twelve-string architecture. Source tuba is realized as an authored BBb yellow-brass Besson Sovereign with piston valves and punchy ensemble phrasing; brass-band tuba context is an editorial supporting-bass registration, not a claim the trio is a brass band. Controlled live room and unprocessed voice are authored; no source capture chain or global tuning asserted.

tradition.name: Música tabasqueña
tradition.lineage: Complete instrumental ensemble format specified by the Tabasco Culture Secretariat for its2025 state children’s tamborileros competition: requinto drum, large drum and cane flute, performing three pieces across danza, son and zapateo. The published rules require at least eight participants; three cards represent instrument classes, not three people. No exact distribution or actual winning group asserted. This is the full prescribed instrumental practice, not an arbitrary extracted track or a claim to all Tabascan music. No singer role in the stated inventory; dancers are not invented vocalists. The2026 version adds medium drums and other performances can add turtle shells; neither is silently transferred into the selected2025 specification. Authored controlled live-room realization of the entire published instrumental format. Percussion-led dance parent follows the positive dance/son/zapateo function. Isolated regional flute retains cane construction, seven openings and wax mouthpiece plug; no invented key, hole distribution or concert-recorder geometry. Regional requinto and large drum retain distinct sizes and double heads. Mahogany shell, goat skins and cord tension are editorial choices within the official heritage document’s described construction possibilities, not measured competitor equipment. Regional assemblies are single coherent compound controls; exact dimensions, drum pitches, species of tension cord, sticking patterns and participant distribution remain unspecified. No global equal temperament, amplification or studio hardware asserted. No inherited old-owner alterations.

tradition.name: Musiqi-ye Zanān
tradition.lineage: Complete The Sun Will Rise, Mahsa Vahdat, KKV FXCD422,2016: all21 issued songs, one solo singer. Her artist discography confirms sole voice and melodies setting classical and contemporary Persian poetry. Producer documents naturally present birds, footsteps, distant church bells/background voices, streams and fountains as retained elements across the recordings. These incidental sounds are preserved as ambience, not additional credited instrumentalists, singers or invented edited samples. Ambient people are not assigned a headcount. tradition.name: Muzica ardeleneasca
tradition.lineage: Complete issued Ardeleana track,1:21, on Rumanian Songs and Dances (Folkways FW04387,1958). Collector notes identify Ardeleana pe trei: Moise Zepa of Dobița, Hunedoara plays a six-hole fluier; dancers add shouted or rhythmically declaimed improvised strigaturi. Retain flute and spoken vocal contributions, with unknown number of dancers/speakers. The listed solo flute is accompaniment, not proof of a wholly instrumental solo. Neighboring track handclaps, whistles and fiddles are not transferred here. No sung role is positively described in this track; dancers movement is not an extra instrument. Authored faithful two-family realization of the full issued track, not recreation of1950s recording apparatus. Fluier uses existing six-hole block-flute construction preset labeled Wallachian as an editorial six-hole model, not an assertion of Wallachian regional identity or measured duct construction. Ash body and tight dance articulation are authored; existing hora/sarba articulation is a catalog approximation of lively dance phrasing, not claim this Ardeleana is hora or sarba. Unknown speaker count and tracking remain neutral, with positively rhythmic spoken delivery. No global tuning, source microphone, room or medium asserted. Broad improvOnFrame follows positively improvised verbal calls over the repeating dance metric frame, not a jazz ancestry claim.

Ardeleneasca denotes the Transylvanian regional musical field: the collector distinguishes its central/southern spoken dance calls from northern sung variants, while Romanian Cultural Institute independently names muzica populara ardeleneasca as a regional repertoire including carols, mourning, love, wedding and doina traditions. Existing romanian_folk is a national umbrella whose Maramures exemplar does not restrict its scope; romanian_doina requires free rhythm and romanian_lautari is a professional-musician/taraf field. This regional community overlaps those without equating itself to one rhythm, ethnicity or source performer. Exact creator map names the label but no Moise Zepa membership asserted. Romanian National Library2018 bibliography classifies the whole printed collection under NM3.3.4 Voci a cappella and lists390pages. extras.description: Complete first edition of Cântați Domnului tot pământul, compiled by Vasile Stanciu, Renașterea, Cluj-Napoca2017, ISMN979-0-9009870-6-8, ISBN978-606-607-226-7. Romanian National Library2018 bibliography classifies the whole printed collection under NM3.3.4 Voci a cappella and lists390pages. The Patriarchate newspaper describes389pages and six functional sections combining standardized psaltic and Transylvanian church repertories; this one-page metadata discrepancy is retained, not silently resolved. All sections are included in this new unaccompanied vocal rendition. Full score pages were not inspected; individual voicings, human headcount, original performances and exact interval systems remain unspecified. No instruments inferred from adjacent books or recordings. Romanian-language institutional church-music repertoire spans psaltic chant and Western-influenced harmonic choral practice, documented by the Romanian Patriarchate alongside regional Transylvanian transmission. Existing byzantine_chant explicitly acknowledges Romanian parallel branches but defines Greek-language oktoechos/ison chant; byzantine_psaltic and byzantine_ecclesiastical likewise specify Greek New-Method/monodic practices. tradition.name: Odia bhajan
tradition.lineage: Dr. Sangita Gosain — Bibhu Bandana, complete announced Samarpan2021 recital ensemble,20March2021. ICCR official programme lists Sangita Gosain for Bibhu Bandana, an Odia ode to the Supreme Lord, with Ajaya Kumar Dash on harmonium, Dushmanta Kumar Parida on tabla and Rudra Prasad Parida on flute. All four roles and one singer are retained. This is the complete announced ensemble for that recital, not personnel borrowed from adjacent festival artists or her other recordings. Odia bhajan is the Odia-language devotional repertoire within pan-Indian bhajan and hindu_stuti_bhajan, not an assertion either broad record excludes Odisha. Official Akashvani catalog explicitly publishes Odia Bhajan volumes dedicated to Jagannath; the selected ICCR devotional recital supplies positive regional-language practice. Existing odia_pop overlaps bhajan-derived phrasing but models secular/popular production; this regional devotional-purpose field is narrower than language-pop generally. No distinct instrument list is used as the category boundary and no exact creator membership is asserted. The complete announced quartet is realized with source-unspecified vocal physiology, one authored accompanied solo singer and neutral unspecified flute architecture. Hand-pumped harmonium retains local keyboard/bellows song-support gesture and authored male reed voicing; tabla uses compatible shisham dayan, copper bayan and fresh syahi as authored settings rather than actual players’ measured instruments. No specific raga, tuning, fixed ornament style, flute material or studio gear is invented. Controlled live-room acoustic and unprocessed voice are authored rendition choices; one singer is positively named, while original recording tracks remain unspecified.

tradition.name: Pinoy traditional
tradition.lineage: Hanunóo man — Ambáhan, complete 1:09 track FW04466_124 on the 1953 Folkways release Hanunóo Music from the Philippines. The issuer credits one unnamed lead vocalist. Original field notes identify Side II Band13 as a lover’s chant, give the complete short courtship verse, and describe its three-note recitation, lengthened line endings and terminating lowered voice. Postma’s firsthand Hanunóo study explicitly distinguishes unaccompanied ambahan from guitar-accompanied urukay; this is not an arbitrary removal of album instruments. All other album tracks, including separately identified flute/fiddle and instrumental ensembles, lie outside this complete-track scope. Release year does not assert an exact recording date. The creator Pinoy traditional field expressly includes Hanunóo man alongside rondalla/dance ensembles, Kulintang and Magindanaon epic chant, establishing a multi-regional traditional Philippine umbrella. The selected unaccompanied Hanunóo poetic practice is a positive branch outside the actual existing kulintang gong-ensemble identity, Filipino harana guitar-serenade formation and kundiman minor-to-major triple-meter art-song structure. Their repertoires can overlap this national field; no claim of mutually exclusive geography or ethnicity. Existing Pinoy indie/pop/rock categories describe modern popular networks, not the full traditional field. A courtship theme alone does not make the selected indigenous recitation identical to harana or kundiman. Broad balladPoetry follows the source’s complete intimate poetic courtship recitation. No worship, chord sequence, drone or equal-temperament inference. Existing voice retains the sole singer; single-lead solo-unaccompanied and free-rhythm recitative are supported by the source, with neutral unspecified physiology, ornament inventory, exact pitch system and tradition controls. The field notes’ three-tone observation is preserved as evidence, not mistranslated into a catalog pentatonic or Western tuning preset. Exact intervals and original equipment are not reconstructed. Moderate effort, neutral tract and a controlled live-room rendition are authored defaults, not measured source anatomy or recording location. No additional instrumental cards are required for this independently documented unaccompanied track.

tradition.name: Wu Fam
tradition.lineage: Royal Fam artist-issued I Am Wu-Tang mixtape (2024), complete separately issued La Saga acapella version, track16. Explicit five-person credits: Dreddy Kruger, Prodigal Sunn, Timbo King, Akhenaton and Shurik'n. Single composite voice card retains the five named rappers. Original instrumental and live versions are separately listed; this is the complete released vocal-only version, not researcher-removal of the backing from the original. Other mixtape guest lists are not imported into this separate edition. Wu Fam identifies the Wu-Tang affiliate network, positively documented by this artist-issued Royal Fam/SunzOfMan/IAM collaboration and creator cluster. Exact creator playlist includes Timbo King, Prodigal Sunn and Royal Fam. Existing east_coast_hip_hop_classic already includes Wu-Tang, so no historical exclusion is asserted; Wu Fam is a narrower artist-affiliation network, not all East Coast rap or any performer merely influenced by RZA. Hardcore hip-hop is a delivery/production category, while the affiliate network includes collaborations and separate vocal-only releases. French guests here do not become permanent Wu-Tang members by participation. Broad mcRhythm describes the selected rap collaboration without pretending all voices are American. Five credited performers retained; voice physiology, lineage and exact pitch mechanism stay source-unspecified. Existing live-group/live-ensemble controls are an explicitly authored combined unaccompanied rendition of all five performers, not an assertion that the issued studio acapella was recorded simultaneously or without overdubs. No fixed beat, sampler or synthesizer is inferred from production credits; no accompaniment is invented. Controlled live room and unprocessed voice are representative choices, not source-session facts; optional tuning and apparatus omitted.

tradition.name: Yaoi
tradition.lineage: Complete Yamaha Music Entertainment Holdings intermediate solo-piano arrangement of Fuyu no Hanashi by Given, arranged/transcribed by Kiyomi Kojima, publisher score432440. Publisher identifies piano solo, J-pop and the Given anime insert song; selected programme is the whole separately published arrangement, not a claim that the original band recording lacks voice, bass or drums. One piano player and zero separate singers in this instrumental score. Printed song lyrics or composer/lyricist metadata do not establish an additional vocal staff or singer. Exact creator Yaoi map includes Given and Centimillimental. The franchise own2019 announcement explicitly identifies the adaptation as BL comics, and its own music page binds Fuyu no Hanashi to the band and composer. This establishes a male-romance franchise/media repertoire branch, not any real performer sexuality, universal sonic style, or claim all peripheral creator-map artists are BL. Existing anison is the broader anime-title-song field; anime_cv is character-voice performance, Japanese soundtrack is wider screen scoring, Shojo is a different demographic discovery group, and Yuri is a neighboring different franchise grouping. These categories overlap but do not exhaust this specifically evidenced BL-linked repertoire. Published J-pop song arrangement supports functionalSong.eastAsianPop; piano notation alone does not make it classical. Authored melody-and-block-chord pop touch, standard studio upright and its existing size/use choices are editorial realizations, not measured publisher-demo hardware. Controlled live-room rendition without inferred global tuning or source apparatus.
